2: B is at aa:bb:cc:... A caches it
Broadcast — delivered to every host on the LAN (dst MAC ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff)
Unicast — delivered only to the requester (dst MAC = A's MAC)
Host A's ARP cache — before and after the exchange
B's IP → aa:bb:cc:... , learned from the reply

svg.metadata:
# FigDown — figures as text. Spec: https://github.com/FigDown/figdown
figdown 0.1 topology # ARP address resolution (RFC 826): Host A needs the MAC for B's IP. # A broadcasts "who-has", B replies unicast, A caches the mapping. # The broadcast vs unicast distinction is a CLASS (meaning in the label, # dashed is only its presentation, `PRESENTATION-AS-MEANING-CARRIER`) — presentation is never the sole # carrier. "The rest of the LAN" is an external, not an invented node. # # HONEST LIMIT (guide/expressing.md "strict message ordering"): step order rides on # the 1/2 label ordinals, a naming convention; the sequence genre # (`MESSAGE-ORDER-AND-STATE`, closed 0.4) makes it first-class, and this figure stays # figdown 0.1 deliberately for portability. The cache update is a local # action on A, not a message — it rides on the reply label and the prose # (mode 3: figure + prose are one deliverable), not on a self-edge. title "ARP Resolution"
# Semantic classes: delivery scope. Label = MEANING; dashed = presentation # only; the legend derives automatically (spec §2.7, `PRESENTATION-AS-MEANING-CARRIER`). class bcast "Broadcast — delivered to every host on the LAN (dst MAC ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff)" stroke=#dc2626 style=dashed class ucast "Unicast — delivered only to the requester (dst MAC = A's MAC)" stroke=#16a34a
node a "Host A\nwants MAC for B's IP" node b "Host B\nowns the target IP"
# Every other station on the segment hears the broadcast but is outside the # resolution proper: an external, drawn as an open edge end (spec §2.8). external lan "rest of the LAN\n(hosts C, D, ...)"
flow right
# Step 1: A broadcasts the request to the whole segment. The same broadcast # reaches every other station too; they ignore it (short label — detail here # and in the showcase prose). edge a -[1: who-has B? (broadcast)]-> b class=bcast edge a -[1: heard, ignored]-> lan class=bcast
# Step 2: B replies to A directly (unicast); on receipt A caches the # IP -> MAC binding — a local action on A, stated on the label, not a message. edge b -[2: B is at aa:bb:cc:... A caches it]-> a class=ucast
# Hybrid panels: a second figdown section below (multi-section `MULTI-FIGURE-DOCUMENTS`), # not nested under the scene header. Each section has one genre (`GENRE-KEYWORD-ALLOWLIST`).
# --- panel: separate genre section (main-standard hybrid = multi-section `MULTI-FIGURE-DOCUMENTS`) --- figdown 0.1 table table cache "Host A's ARP cache — before and after the exchange" | Moment | Entry | |--------------------|-----------------------------------------| | before the exchange| (no entry for B's IP) | | after segment 2 | B's IP → aa:bb:cc:... , learned from the reply |
